calls.reason: The OECD cases show some reduced skill requirements after automation, but not an increasing pattern of executives devaluing work because of theoretical AI capability despite poor output.

AP reports that Deloitte's AI-assisted report contained fabricated references and a judicial quote, prompting public exposure, revisions and an agreed refund. AI causation remains unconfirmed, but the evidence strongly fits the prediction.

Vox documents faulty G/O articles and cheap production, but management promised editorial review and other publishers withdrew similar content. The evidence does not clearly establish willingness to sacrifice quality for savings.
The studies document hallucinations but mixed performance changes. IBM's survey shows adoption alongside risk concerns, without establishing that executives broadly ignored suitability.
Klarna and Wendy's document automation experiments, but no cited evidence connects customer-service reductions to testing a financial breaking point. Klarna also reports retaining human support.

Screen International describes an AI-scripted experimental feature, while the Los Angeles Times reports continued human screenwriting. Neither settles realistic professional replacement within the unspecified period.
